result.topic_en: Discussion of the very small width of the free edge of the membrane of the oval window and its consequences for the motion of the stapes footplate, concluding that the membrane's elasticity must be very small and the footplate held in equilibrium by other forces.

items.english: If this edge were wider, the vibrations of the stapes footplate would be almost entirely compensated by vibrations of this edge, and only a slight effect would take place on the membranes of the cochlea and of the cochlear (round) window.

items.english: Because of the small width of the edge, the effect of this membrane edge on the stapes footplate will be very different for the different positions of the footplate during the sound motion.

items.quote:
Man muß daher,

items.english: One must therefore assume, if it is not to distort the sound, that the elasticity of the membrane is very small, and that the stapes footplate is brought into the correct equilibrium position not by it but by other forces.
